days.reason: Verse 15 contains a direct reference to the day of judgment and compares the judgment on a city that does not receive the disciples with the judgment on Sodom and Gomorrah. This is a central theme for Judgment Sunday (Christ the King), which focuses on the final judgment and Christ's return.

Verses 22-23 link persecution and endurance to the coming of the Son of Man. This is a prophecy about Jesus' return, which is the main theme of Judgment Sunday. The text emphasizes that history has a goal and that faith must endure to the end.
Verses 32-33 deal with Jesus' role as judge by confessing or denying people before the Father on the day of judgment. This is a direct link to the reality of judgment celebrated on this day.

Verses 40-42 describe how actions toward 'the least' (the disciples) are counted as actions toward Jesus himself, and that this determines the reward. This reflects the parable of the sheep and the goats (Matt 25), which is the main text for Judgment Sunday, where judgment is based on concrete action toward the weak.

The chapter begins with the sending out of the disciples with authority and mission. This is a precursor to the great commission that Jesus gives at the ascension. The theme of being sent out to the nations (verse 18) is central to the liturgy of Ascension Day.

Verses 19-20 promise that the Father's Spirit will speak through the disciples. This is a central theme in Easter time, especially in the period leading up to Pentecost (6th Sunday), where the Spirit as witness and speaker is the main focus. The text emphasizes that believers are not alone in their testimony.

This prepares for the way of suffering, which is the theme of Transfiguration Sunday, where Jesus' third prediction of his passion is often read. The text shows that following entails conflict and suffering.

Verses 34-39 emphasize that Jesus comes with a sword and that discipleship requires taking up one's cross. This is a strong call to self-examination and repentance, which characterizes Transfiguration Sunday and the transition into Lent.

This is relevant for Easter time, especially in the period after the resurrection when the Spirit is given as witness and strength to believers, even though the main text for the 2nd Sunday often concerns Thomas's doubt.

Verse 20 mentions 'your Father's Spirit' speaking through the disciples. This is one of the few texts in Matthew that explicitly mentions the Father and the Spirit in the same context (along with the Son who sends them), which can be linked to Trinity Sunday, even though it is not a main text.

_versions.reason: [major] The link to the 2nd Sunday of Easter is incorrect. The text in verses 19-20 concerns the sending out of the disciples before Easter and the promise that the Father's Spirit will speak through them during persecution. This is not a text about Thomas's doubt or belief without seeing (the main theme of the 2nd day of Easter). The Spirit is mentioned here as a comfort and witness in suffering, not as the gift poured out after the resurrection (which is the theme of Pentecost). This is a weak and misleading link. [minor] The link to Trinity Sunday is very weak. Although the Father and the Spirit are mentioned in verse 20, the context is exclusively about the sending out and persecution of the disciples, not a revelation of God's triune nature. There are much stronger texts for Trinity Sunday (e.g., Matt 28:19). Using this text here is forced. [minor] The link to Transfiguration Sunday is problematic. Transfiguration Sunday marks the transition into Lent, and texts about repentance or Jesus' first prediction of his passion are often read. Matthew 10 concerns the sending out of the disciples *before* the suffering, even though it predicts suffering. The text is more relevant for mission, persecution, and judgment than for the actual transition into Lent. The link to Judgment Sunday is far stronger for this text. [major] Matthew 10 is one of the central sending texts in the New Testament. Although it takes place before the resurrection, it is a direct precursor to the commission completed at the ascension (Matt 28:16-20). The theme of 'sending out' (apostolic mission) is the core of Ascension Day liturgy. The text should be linked to Ascension Day, perhaps as secondary, but it is completely missing from today's tagging. [minor] Verse 20 ('it is not you who speak, but your Father's Spirit') is a strong text about the Holy Spirit's witness. This is a central theme in Easter time, especially in the period leading up to Pentecost (the 6th Sunday of Easter often deals with the Spirit and prayer). The link to 'easter-2' was incorrect, but a link to 'easter-6' would have been more theologically precise regarding the Spirit's role as speaker through believers.
